Last Friday (the 21st), in the judgment of the Hong Kong Alliance case, during the early hours, police took a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing onto a police vehicle and removed her. In response to inquiries, the police said the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or intentionally obstructing police in the execution of their duties," and "seditious intent."

In the early hours of last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue "suspected her clothing had a hint of seditious intent," and took her onto a police vehicle and left. While officers were taking the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "we'll take you to the press area," and stretched the orange cordon line toward Yee Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. On that day, a "court-watching volunteer" who was queued near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

"集誌社" (The Collective) inquired with the police about the reasons for the woman being taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that on August 21, they conducted a security operation in the area around the West Kowloon Court, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or intentionally obstructing police in the execution of their duties," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
